definition-changed.flag: class | of a data item; interface | of an object
definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (4.34) defines class of a data item by PICTURE/USAGE, a predefined identifier or an intrinsic function, as 2023 3.33 does in its note; this rule's 'class' is the object-oriented class (4.33/4.36), not a data class, so the difference reaches nothing the rule governs. §2002:4 (4.110) interface of an object lists the methods with their parameters, returned value and exceptions, word for word 2023 3.109 apart from 'may'/'can'; the rule names an interface as the language construct (§2002:4 4.111 'A grouping of method prototypes'), defined alike in 2023 3.110, so scope is unchanged.

definition-dropped.flag: class definition | in object orientation (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (4.36) 'A compilation unit that defines a class of objects' is word for word 2023 3.35 (the screen's 'newer: undefined' is a miss: 2023 still defines it), so the class definitions the rule reaches are the same. The REPOSITORY paragraph of the containing class definition is the same construct in both.
